correctness.rationale: For z=Box(0), t=Diamond(0), the Dunn test at x=1 gives Box≤Diamond; together with monotonicity and top preservation, only cross-tests on distinct atoms are left. A meet map with z=1 is constant; with atomic z at most one atom can map to 1 and the rest map to z; with z=0 the nonzero images are an injective partial assignment of atoms, or one image 1 and the rest 0. For (z,t)=(1,1), (atomic,≥z), (0,1), (0,atomic), (0,0), the contributions are respectively 1, n(2n+1+2^n), P_n+n, n[(n+1)2^n+n²(n−1)+n], and (n+2)^n+2n^(n+1)+Q_n+n. In (0,atomic t), at most one exceptional Box image outside {0,t} is possible, and it forces all other Diamond atom-values to t; counting the optional extra image t gives the n²(n−1) term per t. With both bottoms zero, two or more active atomic images preclude top at an active Diamond value; inactive Diamond values may be zero or an unused atom, which gives Q_n. Rank one and the unique top-image cases have the separately stated counts. Thus the cases exhaust all maps without double counting. Re-evaluating the sums gives 574, 5054, 70834 and 1332432. Independent exhaustive Python 3 replay: /workspace/branches/6cdb05a3-2239-47e5-9be2-ac8dcf3d9a75/independent_check.py 3 (or 4). It checks all top-preserving maps against the defining tests and explicitly counts fixed pairs under conjugation. For n=3 the counts by cycle type (1³),(2,1),(3) are 574,52,13; for n=4 the counts for (1⁴),(2,1²),(2²),(3,1),(4) are 5054,316,86,62,16. Burnside gives 126 and 325. The uploaded script was inspected, not run. Only n=3,4 are exhaustively computed and only these have a claimed orbit count; the all-n case argument is necessary for the labelled formula.
